newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia budget almost ready for fourth reading - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia budget almost ready for fourth reading - Tass.

text.p: Russia's 1997 draft budget is almost ready for its fourth and final reading, due on January 24, Itar-Tass news agency quoted the head of parliament, Gennady Seleznyov, as saying on Friday.
Seleznyov told Tass that as a result of talks between parliament and the government, the budget's social programme had been "significantly strengthened".
Seleznyov, speaker of the State Duma lower house of parliament, praised Russia's various political forces for ensuring the timely passing of the budget.

Deputies approved the third reading of the budget on December 28 by 243 votes to 117. It envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product. Revenues will be 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditure 529.8 trillion roubles.

If the Duma, dominated by communists and their allies, approves the budget, it must be approved by the upper house of parliament and signed into law by President Boris Yeltsin, before it can come into effect.
